policy: A cohort manifest attests the collection context that assessment rows cannot carry by themselves (docs/PHASE-3-FINDINGS.md). `build_comparison` refuses to compare rows without the operator_controlled_single_run attestation. This cohort adds a stated sampling frame (docs/SAMPLING-FRAME.md): its random stratum is a seeded draw from CMS's own enumeration of acute-care hospitals, every drawn facility was attempted, and every facility that was not graded appears below as a recorded exclusion with its basis and its reason. Exclusions are recorded targets, not findings: `basis` says how far the review went, `reason` says what it found. The two strata must not be pooled into a rate; see docs/SAMPLING-FRAME.md. Contact evidence stays in the local discovery registry and is never published.

collection.description: One serial, operator-invoked run of `mrf-honest scorecard` per target under the default retrieval policy: identified User-Agent with a contact address, HTTPS only, robots.txt fetched and obeyed in code before every request, a per-host minimum interval, conditional revalidation against the verified cache, retry backoff, and the default 1 GiB decoded-size ceiling. One bounded GET per file, with a pause between invocations. The six carry-forward files revalidated against the cache: five returned HTTP 304 and moved no body bytes at all.

sampling_frame.summary: Two strata, each a complete enumeration. Stratum A carries forward every subject published in the 2026-08-14 cohort (6 files, 4 systems) and is a convenience sample. Stratum B is a seeded uniform random sample of 48 facilities drawn from the 3024 acute-care, non-federal, 50-states-and-DC hospitals in the CMS Hospital General Information dataset; every drawn facility was attempted and every outcome is recorded. Cohort-wide totals mix the two strata and are descriptions of this cohort, not estimates.

inclusion: state in the 50 states and DC

sampling_frame.format_rule: A target is graded only where the publication is a CMS hospital JSON document. Format is read from the publication, never from a failed request: the URL's file extension decides where it has one; where it has none, a specific declared media type decides; where the declaration is generic, the retrieved document decides. A hospital publishing a conforming CSV is not a hospital with a problem, and is recorded as an exclusion rather than graded against the wrong profile. A .json publication whose retrieval failed stays in the cohort and is graded F with the dated reason.
sampling_frame.origin_resolution: Neither CMS nor any other public dataset this project found records which website a hospital selected to host its file, so resolving a drawn facility to an origin is the one manual step in the frame. A returned cms-hpt.txt is accepted as the right origin only when one of its location entries names the drawn facility, which makes a correct resolution self-verifying; the MRF URL graded is that entry's. Candidate origins that failed were re-checked against independent sources before the failure was recorded, because a wrong guess that 404s must never be published as a hospital that did not publish. Ten first-pass candidates were wrong and were corrected before anything was recorded; two of the ten publish conforming JSON and are graded here. The origin actually checked is named in every exclusion and in data/frames/2026-08-19.frame.json.

collection.robots: robots.txt is fetched and applied by the fetcher itself (src/mrf_honest/politeness.py, RFC 9309), not by an operator's habit: a 2xx body is parsed and obeyed, a 4xx means no robots.txt exists, and a 5xx or network failure is treated as a complete disallow. Two origins in this cohort's draw were skipped on that rule -- both served a robots.txt whose TLS chain would not verify -- and are recorded as exclusions rather than retried.

discovery.method: `mrf-honest discover` retrieved https://<origin>/cms-hpt.txt for every resolved origin with an identified client; every attempt, including failures, is durable evidence in the local discovery registry. No MRF URL in this cohort was hand-assembled: every graded URL is the one a location entry in a retrieved cms-hpt.txt published for the drawn facility.
